title: First Steps
signs: Nothing can hurt you here more than the drops....
The isles are full of these. Engage carefully.
Rocks from the isle can be used to attack.
brief: Five stretches of coast. Each one asks for one thing you have not done yet.
scope: The practice course. Same cliffs, same sea and same cast as The Fractured Isles, at a fraction of its length and with nothing in it that has not been introduced first. Off the course (see levels/index.json); the title screen's PRACTICE row is the only way in.
teaching_note: Every lesson is taught by the shape of the level, not by a line of text. Nothing here says which key to press. What it does instead is make each stretch impossible to leave until the thing it teaches has been done, and put the first, safe version of that thing before the one that costs you anything. Read left to right: 1 THE SHALLOWS is movement and a gap that cannot kill you - miss it and you land on a rock a jump below, which teaches the jump and the climb in one go. 2 BANDITS opens with the same jump over a real pit, then shuts a gate on the first one: fists, and a bottle to drink afterwards. It is also the one stretch that spells a control out - see `coach` - because a fight is the one thing the shape of a level cannot mime. 3 THE ROCKS puts a hunter at throwing range with two rocks at your feet - shoot him and he reads it coming and guards, throw one and he cannot. 4 THE STAIR is three ledges with a bandit on the top one, met from below and in the air. 5 THE ANVIL is Mark, who walks through anything you trade with him. The flag is past his gate, so it is not a stretch you can run.
ground_note: The same numbers The Fractured Isles is cut with, so the two levels are visibly the same coast. features/world/scenery.gd generates every cliff from `solids` - the art cannot end up somewhere you cannot stand, because it is drawn from the same rectangles the player collides with.
solids_note: [x, top_y, w, h]. The height is how far the cliff runs down toward the sea, not anything the player can reach - fall_y is at 1100 and every mass here is deeper than that. An optional fifth value names a piece of art (bridge, island_large); without one the rectangle is drawn as grassed cliff, which is what all ten of these are.
gates_note: The x of each section's end wall, and the whole reason this level teaches anything: while a gate is shut the camera stops with it at the right edge of the screen and an invisible wall stands on the line. You have not run out of floor, you have run out of level, and the only way on is the enemy standing in it. Walking back is never blocked. Four gates, five sections - the last one ends at the flag instead.
hazards_note: None. The lesson the drop teaches at x1224 is the same one spikes teach and it teaches it better, because the pit is also the first jump you have to commit to.
crates_note: Rocks: breakable, liftable, throwable, [x, ground_y]. Area2D only, never solid, so none of them can block or alter the route - which is why no lesson here depends on one being in the way. The first sits alone in an empty stretch with a bandit visible beyond it: something to hit before something hits back. The pair at 2400 and 2496 are the ammunition for the hunter, set near him on purpose: a rock is heavy, it slows you to a bit over half speed, and an arrow knocks it out of your hands, so the carry has to be short enough to survive.
bottles_note: Milk, [x, ground_y, bars]. The third value is health BAR SEGMENTS, not points. Both sit just after a fight rather than before one, and that is now load-bearing rather than tidy: he spawns on the whole bar and drink() refuses a bottle at full health, so one placed before the first punch would read ALREADY FULL and teach nothing. Worth two segments each - 40 points - so one lands in full on anyone who has taken a bar off.
brews_note: The brown bottle, same shape but against the mana bar. One, at the mouth of THE ROCKS, because that stretch is where the blast is first worth spending and the hunter is about to show you why it is not always the answer.
enemies_note: [x, ground_y, kind]. One per section, in the order they are worth meeting: the bandit is an even fight, the hunter has to be answered from range, the second bandit is met from below and in the air, and Mark cannot be traded with at all. No two in one section - this is the course where you get to fight them one at a time.
decor_note: [x, bottom_y, piece]. Art only, never collision. Plants stand on a surface, so their y is the top of the solid under them; vine and vine_rock hang DOWN a cliff face, so their y sits below the lip they hang from. scripts/check_levels.py warns if a standing plant is left in the air after the ground under it moves.
signs_note: Painted on the background, [x, y, heading] or [x, y, heading, subtitle]. Area names and a line of flavour, the same as The Fractured Isles carries - not instructions. No sign names a key; the one place this level spells a control out is `coach`, which is a different thing in a different place. Only the first three stretches are signed at all. THE STAIR and THE ANVIL are deliberately silent: by the time you drop into them you have met a bandit, a hunter and a gate that will not open, and a sign announcing a third fight is telling you what you can already see. Signs are here to introduce things, and they stop when there is nothing left to introduce.
hints_note: The only level in the game that prompts. `hints` true turns on BOTH the cue over a thing you can lift, throw or drink (ui/hud.gd, _drink_prompt) and the `coach` lines below it; every other level leaves it out and shows neither. That is the point of a first level: it teaches the hands - lift, throw, drink, fist, blast - and a game still naming keys on its third level has not taught them. The gate chevron is NOT a hint and stays everywhere: it is the camera answering a question you are asking, not a lesson you have already had. The cost of the rule is that LOAD GAME can drop a first-time player straight into The Dragon's Roost with no prompt on its bottles - accepted, because the course is the way in and the list is for going back to a level you have played.
coach_note:
[x_from, x_to, text, action], read in order and shown one at a time: the first line whose span he is inside and whose lesson he has not had. Each retires itself for good the moment the thing it names has been done once - `jump` on any jump, `strike` on any swing that is not a blast, `blast` on any blast - and all three are lifetime counters, so a retry does not put a lesson back. The text is KEY / VERB and ui/hud.gd splits it on the slash to letter the keycap.

JUMP, 240..560. The first pit opens at 549 and he spawns at 120, so the line is up for the whole walk toward it and gone the moment he leaves the ground. A gap does mime the jump - you cannot get past one without working it out - but it mimes it while standing on the edge of a fall, and this is the first thing the game asks anyone to do.

STRIKE then BLAST, both 1392..2112. A fight is the one thing shape cannot mime at all: you can stand in front of a bandit all day without discovering that J is a fist. The span is the bandit's whole stretch, from the landing at 1392 to his gate at 2112, which puts the first line on screen beside the rock at 1524 - something to hit before something hits back.

A line steps aside while the action cue under it is already naming the same key: with that rock over his head the cue reads J / THROW, so J / STRIKE waits until his hands are empty. Nothing is retired by that - it comes straight back.
